steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: Dear Mom and Dad, It's been so long since I last saw you. How's everything in Velvet Valley?

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: Summer here is nearly over, and Désir isn't as hot anymore. I miss home so much—how are things there? I hope you're doing well and getting a chance to rest more these days.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: I can't wait to come home once I'm better. We can then spend the fall harvest together in our orchard, like we always do.
[Town center] [Night]

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Cough, cough...
A cool night breeze wafts through the window, carrying the sweet, heady scent of datura flowers. The wind nearly snatches the letter off the desk before the ink dries.
Sheila tightens her collar, a shivering running through her. She gets up to close the window, but the frame bumps against something with a dull thud.
Ouch...!

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: You know, in Désir, children who stay up late get snatched by the boogeyman...
Don't try to scare me with your scary stories. I-I'm not afraid! There's no such thing as a boogeyman...
Liam retorts, rubbing his head with a pout as he peeks into the room. His eyes wander to the letter on Sheila's desk.
Liam can't read, but he spots his name written on it. A grin creeps onto his face—he knows it must be something nice.

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Why aren't you in bed yet? You've got to be up early to sell the papers tomorrow.

steps.speaker: Liam
steps.content: I was just about to go back! But then I heard you coughing, so I came to check up on you.

steps.speaker: Liam
steps.content: Hasn't Miss Vautour Bleu told you when you can go to DisCity yet? I bet they have great doctors there who can make you better! Maybe I can ask her... or just let you have my spot... Ow!
Before he can finish, Sheila gives him a light tap on his head.

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Don't be silly. A chance to go to DisCity with the merchant caravan is too precious to waste. You want to see your mother again, don't you?

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Miss Vautour Bleu has already done so much for us. We should trust her plan and not make things harder for her.

steps.speaker: Liam
steps.content: Okay... Once we're all in DisCity, we can figure things out then.
Sleepiness finally overtakes Liam. He lets out a wide yawn, rubs his eyes, and leaves. As the air grows silent once more, Sheila returns to her writing under the soft glow of moonlight.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: It's just a temporary stay in Désir though, I've come to cherish everything here and love the life I've found.

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: It feels just like the beautiful DisCity, only smaller but better perhaps, offering a glimpse of all the wonders that await me ahead.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: It's chilly out. What are you doing by the window all alone? Did Liam wake you?
Alba has just finished her shift at the diner, her dance skirt still hitched up from work.

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: No, he didn't wake me. Liam is a sweet boy. I just couldn't sleep, so I'm writing a letter to pass the time.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: Aww, good to hear. Well, I'm gonna go back then. You know, I'm so tired that I want to grab some beauty sleep the minute the sun goes down, if not for Juan—that idiot got plastered again and threw up all over the flower bed. Had to drag him back home.

steps.speaker: Alba
steps.content: Such a shame about the datura flower—it got completely ruined. I'll have to ask Primrose to help me replant one tomorrow. Where is she, by the way?
Sheila glances over at the bed behind her, where a girl is peacefully sleeping.

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: Shh... she's asleep. I'll tell her in the morning.

After seeing Alba off, Sheila still finds herself wide awake. A metallic taste lingers in her throat, each breath growing more labored. She takes a deep inhale, but even Désir's familiar floral scent brings no relief to her discomfort.

steps.speaker: Sheila
steps.content: (Cough) Soon... soon, we'll all be in DisCity, right...?

steps.speaker: Letter
steps.content: Miss Vautour Bleu's caravan will take us to the shore where hope awaits.
Sheila knows sleep won't come tonight. She carefully folds the letter and tucks it into her pocket. Taking care not to wake Primrose, she tiptoes out and heads to the post office in the downtown.

The night blankets Désir in a deep, still silence. The shops are closed, Alba's lights are out, and Liam, asleep, murmurs for his mother. Juan snores fitfully, clutching the wooden girlfriend he carved for himself.
Sheila walks in the silver moonlight, savoring the tranquility—until some faint whispers suddenly shatter the silence...
[Fade to black]
<color=#fb9259>Leave... now... Leave...</color>
Is someone else awake at this hour? The voice, though unrecognizable, feels disturbingly familiar. Sheila hesitates, then starts searching for its source.
<color=#fb9259>Stop dreaming...</color>
The eerie whispers persist. In the dark, Désir suddenly feels alien to Sheila. She sees nothing ahead, yet the voice sounds unnervingly close.
She freezes, torn between curiosity and a sense of impending danger. But just as she makes to turn back...
A soft "plop" echoes behind her. A datura flower falls from its stem, withering unnaturally fast as it lands on the stone pavement.
Meanwhile, a shadow looms inches away.
Before the girl can even react, the malevolent presence howls and lunges at her.
